BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO AUG 21 MA. THERESA J. BAGAMASBAD 26 Diamond St. Banaba, San Mateo, Rizal Dear Ms. Bagamasbad. This has reference to your letter dated 1 February 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion and clarifications on the issues and concerns like filing a case. Per the representation, you have gone through frantic experiences with your present neighborhood. You filed a complaint against a lupon member and a member of sanggunian barangay, however, they purposely hid the blotter against them. You also mentioned that you filed a complaint in the barangay but two policemen and some barangay tanods took turns in harassing you not to file the complaint. That said barangay tanods were retaliating against you by throwing broken pieces of bottles and cigarette butts inside your front yard, and shouting ugly remarks towards you. Thus, you are hoping that you could be given legal advice in filing of cases, and on what you should refrain from doing in order for your complaint to stand in court. At the onset, please be informed that you may file a complaint directly to the proper tribunals/courts against the barangay officials without the need for Barangay Conciliation. Item I (I) of Circular No. 14-93, dated July 15, 1993, otherwise known as the Revised Katarungang Pambarangay Law provides: l. All disputes are subject to Barangay conciliation pursuant to the Revised Katarungang Pambarangay Law (forrnerly P.D. 1508, repealed and now replaced by Secs. 399-422, Chapter VII, Title l, Book Ill, and Sec. 515, Title l, Book IV, R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1 991), and prior recourse thereto is a pre-condition before filing a complaint in court or any government offices, except in the following disputes: xxxx 1. Where one party is a public officer or employee, and the dispute relates to the performance of his official functions; Xxxx" (Emphasis supplied) In the matter at hand, considering that the respondents in your complaint are barangay officials/employees, and that the subject dispute relates to the performance of their "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

official functions as lupon members, you may directly file your complaint to the proper tribunals without subjecting the case to barangay conciliation. Notwithstanding, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: TOR R. LLAMAS secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs SELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLDnasm Page 2 of 2
